description: EXAMPLE FILE - copy this to repo-map.json and replace the repos/entries below with your own. Version-controlled mapping from content/ source paths (written by export.js) to target repos' docs/ folders, consumed by scripts/distribute.js. This file is hand-written and version-controlled, not generated by any export - it is the input to the distribution script, not its output.
resolutionRule: For a glob source ending in '/**', strip the trailing '/**' to get the source root; each matched file's destination is destDir + '/' + (file path relative to that source root). For a single-file source, the destination is destDir + '/' + basename(source). Destination paths are always relative to the target repo's docs/ folder.

your-org/repo-1.note: EXAMPLE: a live deployed app. pushMode is 'pr' (the safe default) until you've live-verified this repo's deploy trigger genuinely excludes docs/-only commits - see README.md's Setup Walkthrough, step 'Audit each target repo's deploy trigger'. Do not flip this to 'direct' based on documentation alone; verify against the actual platform dashboard (Vercel/Netlify/Coolify/etc.).

your-org/repo-2.note: EXAMPLE: another target repo, same reasoning as repo-1. Each repo gets its own audit and its own note - don't assume a shared deploy platform means a shared answer.

your-org/repo-3.note: EXAMPLE: a repo with nothing that deploys from it (e.g. a docs/content-only repo). Cleared for direct push immediately since there's no deploy trigger to accidentally fire - no audit needed for repos in this category.

entries._comment: Glob mapping: every file under content/product-a/ lands under repo-1's docs/, preserving the relative path (e.g. content/product-a/setup.md -> docs/setup.md).
One source can fan out to multiple target repos - useful for reference material that's genuinely shared across services.
Single-file mapping (no trailing /**): only its basename is used, so this lands at docs/overview.md regardless of its content/ path.

entries.reason: EXAMPLE: meta/planning content that documents this pipeline itself (or is otherwise not reference material any target repo's Claude Code session needs). 'excluded' entries exist so every content/ path is accounted for on purpose, not silently dropped - see README.md's Lessons learned section.
